texts.facts: Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation. While the claimant was riding his Motor cycle on Renugunta-Srikalahasti Main Road (NH-71 Road), when he reached Ayyappaswamy Temple, near Iskathageli Village, Yerpedu Mandal, Tirupathi Urban District, at that time, a Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-01 AD-8247 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety, dashed against the Motor Cycle ridden by the claimant and knocked him down and ran over his left leg causing serious crush injuries to his left leg. Immediately he was shifted to nearby hospital at Srikalahasti and after administering first aid treatment, Sri M Mani vs Sri A Gulsar on 19 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115019795/ 2 During the course of treatment the claimant expended about Rs.6,00,000/- towards medicine, treatment, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges. 3. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the claimant had to undergo amputation of left leg above the knee, due to which he has encountered permanent physical disability, sustaining enormous financial loss, irreparable emotional and mental trauma and pain having undergone during the period of treatment. 4. Respondent No.1 remained absent despite service of notice. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed statement of objections admitting the policy of Insurance with the Lorry. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.9,48,000/- and fastened the liability against the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company and directed to pay the same within a period of 60 days.
texts.arguments: It is also contended that the Tribunal has committed gross miscarriage of justice by not appreciating the materials on record and considering the present facts of the case, NC: 2024:KHC:2619 whereas the claimant has lost his left leg above the knee due to amputation and has not taken the disability as 100% despite the Sri M Mani vs Sri A Gulsar on 19 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115019795/ 3 the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant that reduction of the disability to 20% by the Tribunal ignoring the evidence of the expert Doctor PW.2, who assessed the permanent disability at 80% to the whole body is grossly erroneous, as the Tribunal cannot sit over the judgment and opinion expressed by the Doctor, who is an expert in the field of medicine.

Under such circumstances, when there is no proof of income,

The Doctor has assessed the permanent disability to an extent of 80% to the whole body.
